ORIENTATION
How this course works
AI OFF

ORIENTATION · THE SHAPE OF THE TERM

You will run a company, every week, for ten weeks.

THE SIMULATION

Your board

Your group governs one cross-border
company all term, meeting a new legal
problem each week through its eyes.

THE RHYTHM

Four blocks

From next week: a short quiz, a whole-
class debate, a board case with AI in a
set role, and a live defence — every
week, the same shape.

THE POINT

Two skills

Critical thinking first, storytelling
second — arguing the same facts well
from any side.

THE METHOD

Four moves, every week

Every case in this course is worked with the same four-
move spine: name what's really being decided → find
the line → weigh both lenses → decide with conditions.
Each week dresses the four moves in that week's law. You
will run them for the first time today — without being told
you are doing it.

THE ASSESSMENT

Nothing today counts

Weekly quizzes and in-class board cases (each best 6 of 8),
a midterm on Weeks 1–5, and a final-week capstone: a
live, paired negotiation with no AI and no computers.
There is no final exam. Today is ungraded — deliberately.

WHY IT IS BUILT THIS WAY
The law you will use in your career will have changed by the time you get there. The method — reading facts closely, arguing
every side, deciding with reasons — will not. This course grades the method.

Testable: the weekly rhythm is quiz → debate → board case (AI in a declared role) → live defence; the master method is the same four moves
every week — name the decision, find the line, weigh both lenses, decide with conditions; there is no final exam, and the capstone is a
paired negotiation with AI prohibited.

ORIENTATION
How we use AI
AI · declared roles

ORIENTATION · AI IN A DECLARED ROLE

AI is a partner you out-think — never a substitute for
thinking.

THE RULE

Always a declared role

Each week AI has one job — this week and next, a 
research assistant that gathers and organises. The role
changes as the term hardens: later it will argue against
you, map rights, scout enforcement. In the final session it
is barred from the room entirely, with one declared role
left in preparation only.

THE HABIT

Ask AI, then disagree

Every week from Week 2 you write a short paragraph, by
hand (150–200 words): what AI said, and where you push
back — where it was wrong, thin, or overconfident. The
judgement stays yours, and the paragraph is individually
assessed.

WHY THE RULES ARE STRICT
Not because the tool is forbidden — because undeclared use teaches you nothing and declared use teaches you
everything. The course's bet is that after ten weeks of using AI in its lane and disagreeing with it in writing, you can out-think
it. The capstone tests exactly that.

Testable: AI always operates in one declared role per week, beginning as research assistant; the weekly "Ask AI, then disagree" paragraph
is handwritten, 150–200 words, individually assessed, and runs from Week 2; at the Week 10 capstone AI is prohibited in the room.

SKEMA Global BBA · Business Law (International) · Week 1 · orientation

ORIENTATION
What a case week looks like
AI OFF

ORIENTATION · THE PROMISE

From next week, your board gets a file.

THE DOSSIER

Your company's own dispute

A file about your company: how the fight started, where things
stand, and what people are saying — told by partisan voices,
never a neutral narrator. Nobody in the file is objective. Reading
past that is your job.

THE CONTRACT FILE

Two clauses, read word by word

Every dossier carries two verbatim contract extracts. One of
them is the clause the fight is actually about. The other is a trap
— plausible, professional, and not the point. Telling them apart
takes reading, not guessing.

THE QUESTIONS

Withheld until the laptops close

You research with AI in its declared role — but the questions you
must answer arrive on paper only after devices are away. What
you did not genuinely understand, you cannot answer.

THE MORNING TWIST

Something happens on the day

Each case carries a development printed only on the questions
page — new that morning, impossible to prepare for. Your
analysis has to survive it live.

WHY IT IS BUILT THIS WAY
Every mechanism above exists for one reason: so that the work AI can do for you is never the work that is marked. The
tool can gather; it cannot read your file closely, sit in your board's chair, or defend a judgement out loud. That part was
always going to be you.

Testable: a case week's dossier is told by partisan voices with no neutral narrator; it carries two verbatim contract extracts of which one is a
decoy; the questions are withheld until devices are away; and a morning development, printed only on the questions page, must be
answered live.

pages.english:
DIAGNOSTIC
The opening dilemma
AI OFF

DIAGNOSTIC · NORTHWIND INDUSTRIES

Northwind's plant discharges an effluent into
the river that runs past it. Where the plant sits,
the discharge is entirely legal — permitted,
monitored, within local limits, and standard
practice among local rivals. In Northwind's
home country, the same discharge is banned as
harmful, and it is banned in several others. No
regulator forces Northwind's hand: the local
law simply permits what the home law forbids.
Downstream, a community lives with the river
it is given. A junior manager inside the plant
has now objected — not in court, because there
is nothing to sue over, but to the board, in
writing, on conscience.

— The board must decide what to do. So must you.

DISCUSS
It is legal. Is that the end of the matter — or only the beginning? Take
a first position before we open it up.

HOLD THIS CASE
Northwind returns at the very end of this course, in Week 10, when the same shape — lawful, profitable, and paid for by
people who are not in the room — appears again with real money on the table. What you say today is the baseline you will
be measured against, by yourself.

SKEMA Global BBA · Business Law (International) · Week 1 · diagnostic

pages.english:
DIAGNOSTIC
Three questions underneath
AI OFF

DIAGNOSTIC · WHAT THE DILEMMA IS REALLY ASKING

One decision, three questions that run the whole
course.

Sources of law

Where does the rule that "permits" this
even come from? Law is not weather —
every rule has an origin: a statute
passed by a legislature, a constitution
above it, a regulator's standard, a
court's decision, or long custom.
Naming the source is the first step in
knowing how solid a rule is, and who
could change it.

Legal systems

Why is the same discharge legal in one
country and banned in another?
Because countries answer the same
question through different legal
machinery — and a company operating
across borders cannot simply pick the
answer it prefers. Week 2 installs the
two great traditions behind this
disagreement.

Law & morality

Is "legal" the same as "right"? A valid
law tells you what you may do; it has
never fully answered what you should.
The gap between the two is where every
hard decision in this course lives — and
where Northwind's board is standing
now.

KEEP THE THREE APART
"Where does the rule come from?", "whose rule applies?", and "is the rule enough?" are three different questions. Most bad
arguments about Northwind come from answering one while believing you have answered another.

Testable: the three foundation questions are sources of law (every rule has an identifiable origin — statute, constitution, regulation, case
law, custom), legal systems (different countries lawfully answer the same question differently), and law versus morality (a law can be valid
and still not settle what one should do).

SKEMA Global BBA · Business Law (International) · Week 1 · diagnostic
7
pages.chinese:
诊断 AI 不可用 下的三个问题 诊断·困境真正要问的是什么 一个决定，三个问题贯穿整个过程 当然。法律渊源 “允许”这个的规则在哪里？甚至来自？

法律不是天气—— 每条规则都有起源：法令 由立法机关通过，公司章程 在它之上，监管者的标准， 法院的判决，或长期的习惯。命名源是第一步 知道规则有多可靠，以及谁 可以改变它。法律制度 为什么同一放电在一次中是合法的 国家和另一个国家禁止？

因为各国的答案都是一样的 通过不同的法律问题 机械——以及一家运营公司 跨境不能简单地挑 回答它更喜欢。第 2 周安装 这背后有两个伟大的传统 分歧。法律与道德 “合法”就等于“正确”吗？有效 法律告诉你可以做什么；伊萨斯 从来没有完全回答你应该回答的问题。

两者之间的差距无处不在 本课程中的艰难决定——并且 诺斯风的木板所在的地方 现在。保持三者分开 “规则从何而来？”、“谁的规则适用？”和“规则是否足够？”是三个不同的问题。

最糟糕的是 关于Northwind的争论来自于在回答一个问题的同时相信你已经回答了另一个问题。

可检验：三个基本问题是法律渊源（每条规则都有可识别的起源——法令、公司章程、条例、案例 法律、习惯）、法律体系（不同国家对同一问题的合法回答不同）以及法律与道德（法律可以有效） 但仍然没有解决应该做什么）。

SKEMA Global BBA · 商法（国际） · 第 1 周 · 诊断 7

BLOCK C · LAPTOPS OPEN — AI IN ITS FIRST DECLARED ROLE

Before you take a seat at Northwind's table, find out
what the world already knows.

TASK 1

The practice

How common is it for an industrial
practice to be lawful in one country and
banned in another? Find one real
example — any industry — and note
who defended it, and how.

TASK 2

The argument

Find the argument, made famous by
Martin Luther King, that a law can be
valid and still be unjust. Put it in your
own words — one sentence. Do not

The company

HOW TO USE THE TOOL — THE COURSE'S WAY, FROM DAY ONE
Ask AI to gather and organise: examples, arguments, background. Then do the part it cannot: decide what the material
means for Northwind. Notice, as you work, where the tool is confident and thin at the same time — that observation is the
seed of the "Ask AI, then disagree" habit you start next week. When the briefs are handed out, devices go away and stay

The six seats

Six seats at Northwind's table. You will argue from one
of them — not as a lens, as a person.

SEAT 1

Senior management

You built this plant, you answer to the
owners, and everything you do is
lawful. The objection threatens jobs,
contracts, and a plant that follows
every rule it is given.

SEAT 2

The junior manager

You saw the discharge figures and the
home-country ban side by side, and
you raised it. You have a career, a
mortgage, and a conscience — and only
one of them is in writing.

SEAT 3

The community downstream

You live with the river Northwind leaves
you. Nobody asked you, nobody
compensates you, and the law of your
own country says nothing wrong is

SEAT 4

The home-country regulator

Your country banned this discharge
because the evidence said harm. Now a
company that calls your country home

SEAT 5

The ethicist

You are asked the question everyone
else is avoiding: not "is it legal?" but "is
it right?" — and you must answer it
without pretending the law does not
exist.

SEAT 6

The journalist

You hold the story. Print it, and jobs
may go and the plant may close. Sit on
it, and the river stays as it is. Your duty
is to the truth — but which telling of it?

TEN GROUPS, SIX SEATS — FOUR SEATS ARE DOUBLED, ON PURPOSE
Two groups holding the same seat will reach the debrief with different reasoning. When that happens — and it will — you
have seen the deepest thing this course teaches: a perspective is not an answer. It is a place to reason from.

BLOCK D
The four questions on every brief

BLOCK D · EVERY SEAT ANSWERS THE SAME FOUR

Different chairs, identical questions. That is what
makes the answers comparable.

1 · Read it from your seat

What does this decision look like from where you sit? What do

From your seat: is "it's legal" the end of the matter? Say

The host country permits; the home country forbids. Which rule

Say what Northwind should do. No fence-sitting. Then say,
honestly, what your choice costs and who pays it — every
option here has a bill.

A strong answer argues the seat at its strongest, even if you privately disagree with it — and names the best objection

changes for the next nine weeks.

DIAGNOSTIC
The core tension · the anchor
AI OFF

DIAGNOSTIC · WHERE THE ROOM TURNS

"It's legal" against "legal isn't right" — staged as two
people, not two slogans.

SEAT 1 · SENIOR MANAGEMENT

The letter of the law

A company obeys the law of each place it operates — no
more, no less. It should not impose one country's values
on another that has lawfully chosen differently. If the
discharge is permitted here, the matter is closed. There is
certainty in that, humility even, and a clear line of
accountability: change the law, and we will follow it.

SEAT 2 · THE JUNIOR MANAGER · THE ANCHOR

The moral view

The argument Martin Luther King pressed: a law can be
perfectly valid and still be unjust, and "it was allowed"
has never excused everything that was once allowed.
Permission is not obligation — nothing forces Northwind's
hand but its own choices. A company has a conscience
because its people do, and one of them is saying so out
loud.

THE INSIGHT TO HOLD
Both seats carry a real worry — imposing values on another country (Seat 1) and hiding behind permission (Seat 2). They are
answering different questions: what may we do, and what should we do. The whole course lives in the gap between those
questions, and the skill is arguing both honestly before choosing.

Testable: the anchor of Week 1 is the distinction between a valid law and a just one — the argument associated with Martin Luther King;
"legal" answers what a company may do while "right" asks what it should do; both poles of the tension carry a legitimate concern, and
they are different questions rather than opposite answers.

ORIENTATION
The method you just ran
AI OFF

ORIENTATION · THE REVEAL

The four questions on your brief were the course's
method, unnamed.

Read it from your seat

was Move 1 — name what's really being decided. Before
anything else: what is actually the question, and for whom?

Legal versus right

was Move 2 — find the line. Locate exactly what the rule settles
and where it stops — the line between what is answered and
what is still open.

Whose rule

was Move 3 — weigh both lenses. Two legitimate framings of
the same facts, held up honestly against each other before
choosing.

Commit, and price it

was Move 4 — decide with conditions. A position, its cost, and
who pays — never a verdict pretending to be free.

FROM NEXT WEEK
Each week dresses these four moves in that week's law — and from the drafting weeks onward, the fourth move sharpens
into something harder: fixing, in writing, the thing that failed. Same spine, ten different bodies. By Week 10 you will run it
from blank paper, from memory, with no machine in the room.

Testable: the master method is four moves — name what's really being decided, find the line, weigh both lenses, decide with conditions;
Week 1's four brief questions are this method in plain words; each subsequent week specialises the same four moves to its own doctrine.

CLOSE
The bridge you carry forward
AI OFF

WEEK 1 · WHERE WE STARTED

Today, "legal" and "right" came apart in your
hands, and you argued Northwind's decision
from six chairs that were not yours. That is the
whole course in miniature: see clearly, weigh
honestly, argue every side, then choose — and
know the difference between what the law
allows and what you owe.

The law told Northwind what it could do. It could not tell Northwind what it should.

CARRY IT
Next week: you saw that countries disagree about the same act. Why?
Because the world runs on two great legal traditions — civil law and
common law — and Week 2 installs the difference that explains almost
everything that follows. Come with your company chosen. The four-
block rhythm begins, and the first "Ask AI, then disagree" paragraph
is due.

ONE MORE THING ABOUT NORTHWIND
Keep your answer from today somewhere you can find it. In Week 10, with money on the table and your own signature at
stake, you will meet this exact shape again — and the only person checking whether your answer changed will be you.

因为世界以两大法律传统为基础——民法和民法 普通法——第 2 周安装了几乎可以解释的差异 接下来的一切。与您选择的公司一起来。四个- 区块节奏开始，第一个“问AI，然后不同意”段落 到期了。关于Northwind的另一件事 把今天的答案放在你能找到的地方。
